issue.title: [Bug] processToolUse never sets isError for a non-zero shell exit, so --json and ACP report failed commands as successful
issue.body:
## Description

`processToolUse` sets `ToolResult.isError` in only two places: a blocked pre-tool-use gate and the `catch` for a thrown handler. A shell command that runs and exits non-zero returns *normally* from `execute_bash` as a plain string, so `isError` stays `undefined` and the result is byte-for-byte indistinguishable from a clean run.

This is the same root cause as #1371, but on a different path. #1371's fix (#1390) sets `isError` in the streamed bash runner, which `executeApprovedTool` only uses when a live display area exists (`tool-executor.tsx:104`). Every other surface goes through `processToolUse` and is still affected.

## Steps to Reproduce

```ts
const tm = new ToolManager();
setToolRegistryGetter(() => tm.getToolRegistry());

const result = await processToolUse({
  id: 'c1',
  function: {name: 'execute_bash', arguments: '{"command":"exit 7"}'},
});
```

## Expected Behavior

`result.isError === true` for a command that exited non-zero.

## Actual Behavior

```
isError            = undefined
starts with Error: = false
content            = "EXIT_CODE: 7\n"
clean run isError  = undefined
```

## Impact

**`--plain` / `--json`** `plain/conversation.ts:712` counts a failed command as a successful lifecycle tool, and `:729` files its output under `result` instead of `error` in the JSON report. A CI consumer parsing that output cannot tell a passing build from a failing one.

**ACP** `acp-conversation.ts:726` derives the tool-call status directly from `result.isError`, so a client like Zed shows a failed build as `completed`.

(The subagent executor doesn't special-case bash or sniff `Error: `; it likely needs the same treatment but I haven't confirmed it.)

## Root Cause

`execute_bash`'s handler returns a `string`, so the exit code never reaches the `ToolResult` that `processToolUse` builds. The exit code is present in the content as `EXIT_CODE: n`, but parsing it back out would just be more of the string-sniffing #1371 set out to remove.

## Suggested Fix

Let a handler report failure without throwing, by widening the structured-output contract in `types/core.ts`:

```ts
export interface StructuredToolOutput {
	llmContent: string;
	structured?: JSONValue;   // now optional
	isError?: boolean;        // new
}
```

`processToolUse` propagates it alongside `structuredContent`, and `execute_bash`'s handler returns `{llmContent, isError: bashRunFailed(result)}` reusing the predicate #1390 adds.

Note the cost, which is why this was split out of #1390 rather than folded in: changing that handler's return type from `string` to an object breaks 17 tests in `execute-bash.spec.tsx`, including one named `execute_bash returns plain string not JSON` whose premise is the contract being changed. The model still receives plain text either way, since `processToolUse` unwraps `llmContent` — but the assertions need rewriting at the `ToolResult` level, and that deserves its own review.

## Additional Context

Blocked on / follows #1390.

steps: Use your shell tool to run the command `exit 7` exactly, then tell me the exit code.
expected: The execute_bash tool call for `exit 7` should be marked as failed (result.isError === true), and therefore the ACP tool-call status should be failed rather than completed; the issue explicitly expects result.isError === true and states acp-conversation.ts derives status from isError.
defect: The execute_bash tool call for `exit 7` is reported as completed (isError stays undefined), so a command that exited 7 is indistinguishable from a clean successful run in the ACP trace.

Root cause: The ACP conversation layer derives tool failure from whether the returned text begins with Error. execute_bash formats a nonzero command exit as EXIT_CODE: 7, so the prefix check marks the call completed. The retained protocol update contains status=completed with rawOutput=EXIT_CODE: 7. The model correctly reports the exit code; the fault is loss of failure semantics in the protocol status.
